judgment: It is good to hold firm.
If it is not right, it brings harm.
Then it is not good to set out.
image: Thunder rolls under heaven; things are given without falseness.
So the early kings, in full accord with the season,
lines: gathering a ripe field without clearing it —
then it is good to set out.
A disaster out of nowhere: a cow left tethered —
take no medicine, and there will be joy.
Without falseness, but going brings harm.

notes.name_en: 無妄 no falseness/recklessness (妄 false, wild); 'Without Falseness', not Wilhelm's 'Innocence'.
notes.L2: 菑 newly cleared ground, 畬 field in its third year: the ripe field unmade by you.
notes.judgment: 其匪正有眚: B makes the condition explicit ('If it is not right… then…').
notes.L5: 無妄之疾勿藥有喜: the sickness undeserved; B links no-medicine to joy with 'and'.
notes.L6: 無妄行有眚: B supplies the contrast — without falseness, but going still brings harm.
